paper_title: Thermal Management in Fine-Grained 3-D Integrated Circuits

linked_assets.kind: commercial FEM software website cited as reference 27 (not a code, data, or config artifact)

scenario.figure_or_table: Fig. 4A-B (monolithic 3-D NAND gate thermal profile without heat extraction); geometry and bias in Section IV text; peak temperature reported on PDF page 6
scenario.description: Finite element (COMSOL) steady-state and transient thermal simulation of a transistor-level monolithic 3-D (M3D) NAND gate with two PMOS in the bottom tier and two NMOS in the top tier, joined by 50 nm inter-tier vias, and no heat extraction feature. The paper reports a top-tier peak of about 420 K (roughly 120 K rise); the introduction cites up to 450 K.
scenario.architecture: Transistor-level monolithic 3-D IC, NAND gate; overall area 183x145 nm^2, channel length 16 nm, ILV length 110 nm, total z height 1.4 um, 600x300 nm^2 heat sink under the substrate
scenario.workload: Static NAND gate operation with a 50% duty cycle over a 100 ns period; heat sources at drain and gate blocks
scenario.operating_point: Drain 0.8 V; gate 0.527 V and 0.495 V on the two pull-up transistors; heat sink bottom held at 300 K; all other boundaries adiabatic

original_setup.solver: COMSOL Multiphysics finite element method, coupled Joule heating and heat conduction PDEs, steady-state and transient (PDF pages 4-5)
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper runs no placement or design-space optimizer. It hand-places a thermal junction and a tungsten heat-conducting nano pillar at the top transistor (PDF pages 3, 7).
original_setup.controller: None. There is no thermal or DVFS controller. The only time dependence is a 50% duty cycle over a 100 ns period (PDF page 5).
original_setup.benchmark: Transistor-level monolithic 3-D (M3D) NAND gate, with 2 PMOS in the bottom tier and 2 NMOS in the top tier, joined by 50 nm inter-tier vias. Area is 183x145 nm^2, channel length 16 nm, ILV length 110 nm, total z height 1.4 um, and the heat sink is 600x300 nm^2. The scenario has no heat extraction features (PDF pages 5-6, Fig. 4A-B).

thermal_observable.location: Top-tier transistor of the monolithic 3-D NAND gate, without heat extraction (Fig. 4A-B); the paper calls this about a 120 K rise over 300 K ambient
thermal_observable.aggregation: Peak (maximum) temperature in the FEM steady-state field. The introduction cites up to 450 K for M3D, which is inconsistent with the 420 K in Section V.

physical_mismatches.reason: Nanoscale device-level 3-D FEM (183x145 nm^2 NAND gate, 1.4 um stack) differs in scale from a centimeter-scale 2D floorplan with watt-level block power. It has no block floorplan and no per-block watts; heat comes from transistor I-V Joule heating at the drain and gate blocks. The scenario is not steady_2d_relevant.

Monolithic 3-D stacking: two tiers joined by 50 nm inter-tier vias, with top-tier heating far from the sink. A 2D Studio model cannot represent this vertical tier structure, which is the cause of the hotspot.
No interposer or chiplet system, and no cooling model beyond a 300 K isothermal sink face with adiabatic sides. This differs from package-level heat-sink or cooling models.

Transient behavior is a 50% duty cycle over 100 ns. The scenario has no published power time series, and the paper's transient results are shown only in figures (Figs. 6-7), not as extractable numbers.
The paper's own heat extraction (thermal junction and tungsten pillar) is a design feature, not a controller or optimizer. It is outside the scenario and cannot be reproduced in a 2D Studio runner.
No reliability model. The paper discusses reliability only qualitatively. Nanoscale conductivity reduction (Si nanowire 13 W/m/K) and quantum effects are simplified or ignored.

studio_assumptions: No Studio package or material assumptions are recorded here, because the packet has no pinned assets and no Studio bundle specification.

Dimensions and powers do not support a placement. A separate illustrative 2D placement could be constructed only if the runner has dimensions and powers; its coordinates would be generated, not paper-derived, and its temperatures could not be compared numerically to the paper's 420 K.
missing_inputs: Floorplan blocks (x_m, y_m, width_m, height_m) are not published for any scenario. The packet gives overall area and tier layout only, so the floorplan is left empty.
Same-scenario power_rows (name and watts) are absent. The paper gives bias voltages (drain 0.8 V, gates 0.527 V and 0.495 V) but no per-block or total watts or currents, and no rule to derive power.
Table I (device materials and dimensions) on PDF page 4 contains no extractable text, so per-block dimensions and material properties are unavailable.
No pinned assets: the assets list is empty. The only linked resource is the COMSOL website (www.comsol.com, PDF page 8), a commercial software site, not code, data, or config.
No power time series or published transient numbers; Figs. 4-7 are figures only, and any digitized values would carry uncertainty.
COMSOL model files, mesh, and boundary and material configuration are unavailable.
The 420 K (Section V, PDF page 6) and 450 K (introduction) peak values conflict, and the paper does not say which setup yields 450 K.
